name: Busan
operatingHours: Busan Metro (Lines 1–4) runs ~5:30 AM–~midnight daily; last trains leave central stations around 11:30 PM–midnight. Trains every 3–6 min by day, 8–10 min late evening. No all-night service; the Busan-Gimhae Light Rail and Donghae Line have their own, slightly different hours.
fareInfo: Distance-based: ₩1,600 (up to 10 km) or ₩1,800 (longer) with a T-money, Cashbee or Hanaro card (2026; single-use QR tickets cost ₩100 more). Metro 1-day pass ₩6,000 and 3-day ₩13,000 (Lines 1–4 only; not valid on the Donghae Line or the airport light rail). Tap the same card on buses; transfers within 30 minutes are free.

lines.name: Busan–Gimhae Light Rail
lines.firstLast: Gimhae Airport ↔ Sasang (Line 2): ~5:30 AM to ~midnight, ~10 min.

sights.name: Haeundae Beach
sights.note: Korea's best-known beach, a 1.5 km crescent of sand backed by high-rise hotels, with sand-sculpture festivals, summer swimming and a lively seafront strip.

sights.name: Gamcheon Culture Village
sights.note: A hillside neighbourhood of pastel houses stacked up the slope, now an art village with murals, small galleries and a famous Little Prince statue; pick up the stamp map at the entrance.
sights.hours: Village open all day; shops and galleries ~9:00 AM–6:00 PM

sights.name: Haedong Yonggungsa Temple
sights.note: A rare seaside Buddhist temple perched on rocks above the East Sea north of Haeundae, best at sunrise before the tour buses arrive; reach it by bus from Haeundae.

sights.name: Gwangalli Beach & Gwangan Bridge
sights.note: A cafe-lined beach with a clear view of the lit-up Gwangandaegyo suspension bridge at night, plus occasional drone shows and plenty of seafood and bars along the strip.
sights.hours: Open 24 h; bridge lit after dusk

sights.name: Beomeosa Temple
sights.note: A 1,300-year-old mountain temple on the slopes of Geumjeongsan, with tiered halls among tall pines; it is also the start of a hike up to the fortress wall.
sights.hours: Grounds open daily ~dawn to dusk; halls ~6:00 AM–6:00 PM

sights.name: Busan Air Cruise (Songdo Marine Cable Car)
sights.note: A cable car crossing Songdo Bay between the beach and the Amnam Park side, with glass-floor cabins and views of the harbour; best on a clear evening.
sights.hours: ~9:00 AM–9:00 PM (to ~10:00 PM weekends); closed in high winds

sights.name: Jagalchi Market
sights.note: Korea's largest seafood market, where you choose live fish from the stalls and have it cooked upstairs; go for the bustle even if you do not eat.
sights.hours: ~5:00 AM–10:00 PM; many stalls shut on the 1st and 3rd Tuesday

sights.name: BIFF Square
sights.note: The old film-festival street in Nampo, now a lively strip of street-food carts selling ssiat hotteok (seed-stuffed pancakes), with hand prints of film stars embedded in the pavement.
sights.hours: Open all day; food stalls ~11:00 AM–midnight

sights.name: UN Memorial Cemetery in Korea
sights.note: The only UN cemetery in the world, a peaceful memorial park for soldiers of the Korean War with a small museum and beautifully kept lawns.
sights.hours: ~9:00 AM–5:00 PM (to ~6:00 PM in summer); open daily

sights.name: Gukje Market
sights.note: A sprawling traditional market that grew out of the postwar refugee years, with alleys of clothing, kitchenware and bean-pancake stalls beside Bupyeong Kkangtong Market's night food.
sights.hours: ~9:00 AM–8:00 PM; closed 1st and 3rd Sunday of the month

sights.name: Taejongdae Resort Park
sights.note: A forested headland with cliffs, a lighthouse and a walking and tram loop on Yeongdo's southern tip, giving sweeping views over the open sea.
sights.hours: Park open 24 h; Danubi shuttle train ~9:00 AM–5:00 PM

sights.name: Oryukdo Skywalk
sights.note: A glass-floored lookout hanging over the sea cliff at Oryukdo Islets, with views to the white lighthouse and the Gwangan Bridge; free and short, usually combined with the coastal Igidae path.

sights.name: Songdo Beach & Skywalk
sights.note: Korea's first public beach, a calmer family-friendly bay with a skywalk jutting out over the water and boardwalks along the headland, reached from Nampo by bus.
sights.hours: Beach open 24 h; skywalk ~9:00 AM–6:00 PM

sights.name: Igidae Coastal Walk
sights.note: A rugged oceanside trail along the cliffs between Oryukdo and Gwangalli, with sea views of the lighthouse and plenty of fishermen perched on the rocks.

sights.name: Dongbaekseom Island & Nurimaru APEC House
sights.note: A camellia-covered peninsula at the end of Haeundae with a seaside walking loop, a lighthouse and the circular APEC summit building; an easy sunrise or sunset stroll from the beach.
sights.hours: Island open 24 h; APEC House ~9:00 AM–6:00 PM (closed Mon)

sights.name: Yongdusan Park & Busan Tower
sights.note: A hilltop park above Nampo reached by escalator, topped by the 120 m Busan Tower with views over the harbour, bridges and downtown rooftops.
sights.hours: Park open 24 h; tower ~10:00 AM–10:00 PM

sights.name: Haeundae Dalmaji-gil
sights.note: A cherry-lined hill road above the Mipo area with cafes and sea views, popular at sunset and in spring; it is the least touristy stretch of the Haeundae coast.

railStations.name: Busan Station
railStations.note: The KTX terminus: high-speed trains from Seoul in ~2h 40m, plus Mugunghwa/ITX services along the south coast. Metro Line 1 stops at the station and the Nampo/Jagalchi waterfront is two stops away.

airports.name: Gimhae International Airport
airports.transitNote: West of the city. The Busan-Gimhae Light Rail (Airport Station, on the subway map) links to Metro Line 2 at Sasang in ~10 min, then ~35–45 min to Seomyeon or ~50–60 min to Haeundae (~₩1,700–2,500 in total). Airport limousine buses and taxis (~₩25,000–50,000) take 40–70 min.
airports.hours: Light rail: first train ~5:20 AM, last ~11:40 PM (varies by direction).
